name: list_processes
summary: List the running processes ranked by CPU or memory use. Each row shows the PID, whether the program is an Apple/system binary or a user-installed app, its %CPU and %MEM, the owning user, how long it has been running, and the command. Answers 'what's eating my CPU/battery/memory right now' and 'is anything stuck or long-running'. Use sort_by, limit, filter, and scope to narrow the list.

params.name: sort_by
params.description: Rank by 'cpu' (most CPU-hungry first, the default) or 'memory' (largest resident footprint first).

params.name: limit
params.description: How many processes to show (1–100). Defaults to 20.

params.name: filter
params.description: Optional case-insensitive substring; only processes whose command or name contains it are shown (e.g. 'chrome', 'node'). Matched on this Mac, never passed to a shell.

params.name: scope
params.description: 'all' lists every process (the default); 'user' lists only those owned by the current login user.

name: process_info
summary: Show everything known about one process by PID: its full command line, the executable path (the binary responsible for it), the parent process that started it, the owning user, %CPU and %MEM, when it started and how long it has run, its state (including whether it is a zombie/defunct process), whether it is an Apple/system binary or a user-installed app, and whether macOS's launchd auto-starts it. Use list_processes first to find the PID.

params.name: pid
params.description: The numeric process ID to inspect (from list_processes). Must be greater than 1.

name: cpu_load
summary: Report overall CPU pressure: the 1-, 5-, and 15-minute load averages both raw and per-core (load divided by core count, where ~1.0 per core means fully busy), the number of cores, and the top CPU-consuming processes. Use to judge whether the machine as a whole is overloaded, not just one app.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many top CPU processes to include (1–20). Defaults to 5.

name: memory_stats
summary: Report system memory: total installed RAM, how much is used vs. free, and the breakdown into wired (unswappable kernel memory), active, inactive, and compressed pages, plus the top memory-consuming processes. Use to judge memory pressure and find what is holding the most RAM.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many top memory processes to include (1–20). Defaults to 5.

name: gpu_stats
summary: Report graphics (GPU) utilization for the built-in GPU: overall device utilization %, the renderer and tiler utilization %, and GPU memory in use. Note: macOS does not expose PER-PROCESS GPU usage without administrator rights, so this is a whole-device figure; to guess which app is driving the GPU, look for GPU-helper processes (e.g. WindowServer, *.WebKit.GPU) high in list_processes.

name: startup_items
summary: List programs that start automatically, as managed by macOS's launchd service manager (background agents and daemons), showing each one's label, current PID if running, and last exit status. Defaults to third-party items so you can see 'what did I install that auto-starts'. Note: classic Login Items are not included here (they require an Automation permission grant).

params.name: scope
params.description: 'third_party' hides Apple's own com.apple.* items so only software you installed is shown (the default); 'all' lists every launchd-managed item.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many items to show (1–200). Defaults to 50.

name: quit_process
summary: Gracefully quit the GUI application that owns a given PID by sending it the normal Quit command (the same as choosing Quit from its menu), so it can prompt to save and shut down cleanly. STAGED for confirmation; it can lose unsaved work and is not undoable. Only works for GUI apps — for background/daemon processes use terminate_process instead. This never force-kills.

params.name: pid
params.description: The numeric process ID of the GUI application to quit (from list_processes). Must be greater than 1.

name: terminate_process
summary: Ask a background/daemon process to exit by sending it the polite termination signal SIGTERM (the default 'please shut down' signal), letting a well-behaved process clean up before exiting. STAGED for confirmation; it is not undoable. This deliberately never sends SIGKILL (force kill), which would give the process no chance to clean up. GUI applications are refused here — use quit_process for those, so they can prompt to save.

params.name: pid
params.description: The numeric process ID to send SIGTERM to (from list_processes). Must be greater than 1 (PID 1 and below are protected).
